records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2601.11398v1, submitted 16 January 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The paper combines expert qualitative development of help-seeking and topic taxonomies with held-out LLM classifier evaluation and a separate consensus-coded qualitative analysis of security-, privacy-, and safety-related posts.

Research objective.value: Characterize how people seek online help for digital privacy, safety, and security at Reddit scale and build validated classifiers for help-seeking posts and their topics.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: expert-informed mixed-methods analysis with inductive and deductive qualitative coding

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Nine experts defined help seeking from 800 reviewed posts, consensus-labeled a 2,000-post gold set, and developed nine topics from 300 posts; LoRA-tuned Gemini classifiers were evaluated on held-out sets and applied to 89 million posts. A separate two-researcher hybrid analysis of 250 sampled help-seeking posts examined problem structure and resolution.

Domain.value: online digital privacy, safety, and security help seeking

Number of documents.value: 1.1 billion filtered Reddit posts in the source corpus; 89 million posts classified at scale; 2,000 help-seeking gold posts, 750 topic-gold posts, and 250 posts in the qualitative deep dive

Number of participants.value: nine privacy/safety/security experts; two primary qualitative coders plus three structure coders; Reddit authors are not treated as research recruits

Exact model/version.value: Gemini 1.5 Flash for help-seeking classification and Gemini 2.0 Flash for topic classification; dated snapshots not reported

Prompting strategy.value: few-shot baseline followed by LoRA supervised tuning; topic prompts/tuning use one binary decision per theme

Fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation.value: LoRA rank 4; help-seeking model 4,000 steps, batch 2, learning rate 0.0001; topic model 3,000 steps, batch 16, learning rate 0.0001

Human role.value: Experts define constructs, build and adjudicate gold labels, develop the topic taxonomy, inspect wild precision, and conduct a source-level qualitative analysis.

Unit of analysis.value: Reddit post; binary topic labels per post

Generated outputs.value: help-seeking labels, nine topic labels, emotion labels, scale estimates, and qualitative themes about help structures and outcomes

Baselines.value: few-shot Gemini 1.5 Flash baseline and human consensus labels

Automatic metrics.value: accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 on held-out labels; wild precision with confidence interval

Human-evaluation design.value: At least two researchers independently labeled each gold item, then the full team resolved disagreements; the paper intentionally uses consensus and does not report inter-rater reliability.

Principal results.value: The tuned help-seeking model reached F1 90.7%, precision 88.3%, recall 93.3%, and accuracy 93.3% on 300 held-out posts; wild precision was 93.2% (plus or minus 2.76%). The topic model reached overall F1 92.0% across 2,362 held-out binary labels and found 3,010,841 help-seeking posts.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Only public Reddit content was used; private/quarantined communities were excluded, identifying details and verbatim user quotations were removed, and the planned release is a dehydrated URL-plus-annotation dataset.

Author-reported limitations.value: Incomplete and platform-specific crawl, potentially biased gold data, nonuniform classifier errors, compounding errors across classifiers, lack of causal or prevalence claims, and self-censorship/demographic limitations of Reddit.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: deployment recall is borrowed from the curated test set rather than audited among wild negatives; consensus without reliability statistics obscures construct disagreement, and sequential selection/classification can amplify topic and temporal bias.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Strong large-scale example for separating held-out label performance, wild-set audits, qualitative construct formation, and downstream compound-error analysis.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2602.09339v1, submitted 10 February 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The paper makes a multi-agent LLM pipeline the primary inductive thematic analyst of sensitive chatbot-use discourse, but provides no human coding or expert validation and omits essential model and prompt details.

Research objective.value: Characterize self-reported risk, dependency, emotional attachment, and help-seeking in public discourse about AI-chatbot use.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: multi-agent LLM-assisted reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke

Actual operationalized methodology.value: The authors collected 2,428 posts from two risk-focused subreddits, used a multi-agent pipeline said to approximate familiarization, semantic coding, and theme construction, iteratively read an unspecified subset to form 14 categories, assigned one primary theme and supporting phrases to every post, and aggregated categories into five dimensions; humans selected examples but did not independently code or validate the analysis.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: primarily inductive, followed by fixed-category application

Domain.value: AI-chatbot dependency, emotional attachment, psychological risk, and user help seeking on Reddit

Number of participants.value: not reported; public post authors were not recruited and unique-user count is not supplied

Prompting strategy.value: Role-specialized agents for familiarization, semantic coding, and theme construction are described conceptually; prompts, agent count/configuration, context handling, and decoding settings are not reported.

Human role.value: Authors interpret aggregate results and manually select representative cases; no expert human reference analysis or item-level audit is reported.

Unit of analysis.value: Reddit post assigned one primary thematic category

Generated outputs.value: 14 categories grouped into five dimensions, supporting phrases, prevalence summaries, and emotion probabilities

Automatic metrics.value: category frequencies and emotion probabilities from j-hartmann/emotion-english-distilroberta-base; no coding-validity metric

Principal results.value: The model-derived analysis describes five interacting dimensions of dependency-related discourse and emotional patterns, but provides no human-grounded estimate of code/theme accuracy or interpretive validity.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Raw Reddit data are withheld and results use anonymized summaries rather than direct quotations; pipeline and visualization code are linked.

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors caution that risk-focused Reddit communities overrepresent extreme experiences, demographics and clinical status are unavailable, prevalence/causality cannot be inferred, and LLM analysis may miss context and should not replace expert coding.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the unreported model, prompts, agent topology, runs, sample-selection process, and absence of human validation make the thematic findings non-reproducible; a single primary label suppresses co-occurring meanings, and reported category counts appear internally inconsistent with the 2,428-post denominator.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: High-risk negative case motivating minimum reporting standards, human trace audits, multi-label evaluation, and explicit separation of author interpretation from unvalidated agent consensus.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health article, volume 23(1), article 123, published 2026
records.decision_reason: The study uses an LLM to extract and cluster lived-experience submissions and reports a small human comparison, though its numerical validation results and downstream theme audit are missing.

Research objective.value: Identify unmet needs and service priorities in Australian ADHD lived-experience submissions to a Senate inquiry using an AI-assisted analysis.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: AI-assisted thematic analysis of public lived-experience submissions

Actual operationalized methodology.value: GPT-4o-mini extracted problems, services, solutions, and demographics from 480 submissions using five examples; embeddings and agglomerative clustering grouped extractions, a second LLM labeled clusters, and the research team reviewed/grouped clusters into themes and adjudicated ambiguous assignments. Twenty-five separate submissions were used for a three-annotator semantic validation.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid structured extraction plus inductive clustering and human consolidation

Domain.value: ADHD health services and Australian policy submissions

Number of documents.value: 505 eligible lived-experience submissions: 25 validation submissions and 480 analytic submissions, from 701 total inquiry submissions

Number of participants.value: three senior medical-student annotators supervised by a senior clinician-researcher; submission-author count not reported

Model family.value: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini plus an unspecified LLM-as-judge/cluster-labeling model

Exact model/version.value: GPT-4o-mini; dated snapshot and judge/labeler model not reported

Prompting strategy.value: Structured extraction prompt informed by inquiry terms, with five worked examples; separate prompts generated cluster labels and semantic comparison judgments.

Human role.value: Three annotators create comparison extractions; researchers review clusters, group them into themes, resolve ambiguous categories by consensus, and retain final interpretation.

Unit of analysis.value: written lived-experience submission and extracted issue/service/solution statement

Generated outputs.value: structured extractions, embeddings/clusters, cluster labels, themes, and frequency estimates

Baselines.value: independent extractions by three trained human annotators on 25 submissions

Automatic metrics.value: LLM-as-judge semantic agreement is described, but numerical validation scores are not reported

Human-evaluation design.value: Three blinded annotators independently extracted 25 random submissions after training; an LLM judged semantic similarity among human and model outputs. The paper states model agreement was comparable to human agreement but omits values.

Principal results.value: Frequently extracted problems included costs/wait times (46%), specialized care (39%), delays (36%), and gender bias (27%); affordable care was the leading service priority (71%). The claimed human-comparable validation cannot be verified numerically from the article.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: The corpus consists of public Parliamentary submissions; original public authorship was acknowledged, while the article omits identifying information.

Author-reported limitations.value: Self-selection and literacy bias, underrepresented groups, inquiry-term prompt bias, small validation sample, subjective human grouping, possible ordering effects, and incomplete demographics.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: an unspecified LLM may judge outputs produced by the same model family, validation statistics are omitted, validation cases are excluded from the final analysis, and clustering/theme consolidation has no source-trace or independent audit.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Shows why complete validation reporting, independent judges, source-level cluster audits, and end-to-end rather than extraction-only evaluation are required.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed JMIR Mental Health article, volume 13, e90155, published 2026
records.decision_reason: The paper strongly validates an LLM transition-stress rating against an expert panel, then uses an LLM to generate narrative themes; the latter qualitative stage is central but not independently human-validated.

Research objective.value: Develop and validate an LLM-derived veteran transition-stress score and use it to reveal narrative architectures associated with low versus high stress.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: LLM-assisted narrative and thematic analysis following measurement validation

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Ten experts developed a five-point anchored stress rubric and independently rated 20 transcripts. Gemini 2.5 Flash was compared under zero- and few-shot prompting, then zero-shot scored all 106 interviews. A separate targeted 'qualitative researcher' prompt analyzed complete interviews for agency, communion, identity continuity, stereotype threat, redemption/contamination, coping, challenge framing, and gender, comparing low- and high-score groups.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: deductive rubric scoring followed by targeted abductive/thematic interpretation

Domain.value: US military-veteran transition stress and narrative identity

Exact model/version.value: Gemini 2.5 Flash via API; model was locked but dated identifier not reported; temperature 0

Prompting strategy.value: Zero-, one-, two-, three-, and five-shot anchored stress-rating prompts with rationale, followed by a separate structured qualitative-researcher prompt for predefined narrative constructs.

Human role.value: Experts define and calibrate the stress construct and serve as the criterion panel; authors interpret construct correlations and LLM-generated narrative themes and retain clinical authority.

Unit of analysis.value: veteran interview transcript; stress rating and group-level narrative pattern

Generated outputs.value: five-point stress rating with rationale, high/low strata, and narrative-architecture themes

Baselines.value: mean ratings from a ten-expert human panel on 20 transcripts

Number of runs or seeds.value: one reported output per prompt condition/transcript; repeat-run stability not tested

Automatic metrics.value: absolute-agreement ICC, Pearson correlation, MAE, RMSE, construct correlations, group comparisons, and five threshold sensitivity analyses

Human-evaluation design.value: Ten experts independently and blindly rated 20 random transcripts after calibration; human reliability and model-human agreement were quantified.

Principal results.value: Human panel ICC(A,10)=0.978, single-rater ICC=0.817 and alpha=0.799. Zero-shot Gemini-human agreement was ICC=0.954, r=0.955, MAE=0.49 and RMSE=0.61 on 20 transcripts; few-shot examples did not improve performance. LLM stress ratings correlated with clinical measures, while generated narrative themes distinguished low/high groups.

Efficiency or cost results.value: The complete LLM analysis took under 30 minutes versus an estimated 175 to 265 human person-hours; monetary cost not reported.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Participants consented specifically to machine-learning transcript analysis; data were coded, deidentified, and secured. The authors require human clinical authority and reject sole-model diagnosis, benefits decisions, or punitive surveillance.

Author-reported limitations.value: Cross-sectional design, no predictive validation, one model and no repeat-run/cross-model stability, limited post-9/11 and predominantly male sample, narrative self-presentation effects, and need for independent human triangulation of themes.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: excellent agreement on an ordinal stress rubric does not validate the subsequent LLM-generated thematic architecture; that stage uses targeted constructs, excludes the middle-score group, and lacks a blinded human thematic comparator.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Provides a strong construct-validation pattern while demonstrating the need to validate each downstream interpretive stage separately and not transfer confidence from rating to theme generation.

Number of documents.value: not yet determined; protocol searches OSF, ICPSR, Qualitative Data Repository, and Harvard Dataverse

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed Journal of Medical Internet Research article, volume 28, e88677, published 2026
records.decision_reason: The paper directly compares single-researcher inductive thematic analysis with a standardized Claude analysis of the same chronic-illness interviews, but uses an unblinded descriptive comparison with no reliability or run-stability test.

Research objective.value: Compare traditional and LLM-assisted thematic analysis of patient experiences managing multiple chronic illnesses.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: interpretivist inductive thematic analysis and LLM-assisted thematic analysis

Actual operationalized methodology.value: One researcher manually conducted an inductive thematic analysis of 30 interview transcripts with memos and team reflexive discussions. Claude 3.5 Sonnet received each full transcript under the same structured prompt to identify themes, categorize passages, and extract quotations. The same researcher then used predefined qualitative criteria and memos to map convergence and method-unique themes/subthemes.

Domain.value: patient experiences of multiple chronic-illness management

Number of participants.value: 30 adults with at least two chronic illnesses; one primary manual analyst

Exact model/version.value: claude-3.5-Sonnet-20240620; temperature 0, maximum output 8192 tokens, Python 3.10.11

Prompting strategy.value: The same structured prompt was applied to each complete transcript, requesting themes, categorized passages, and illustrative quotations; no conversational calibration or reruns.

Human role.value: A single researcher produces the human analysis, reviews model output, maps convergence/uniqueness and makes all final interpretive decisions, with team reflexive discussion.

Generated outputs.value: themes, subthemes, categorized passages and illustrative quotations

Baselines.value: single-researcher traditional thematic analysis with reflexive team discussion

Number of runs or seeds.value: one reported model analysis per transcript; no repeat-run assessment

Automatic metrics.value: none; comparison was interpretive and descriptive

Human-evaluation design.value: The same manual analyst performed an unblinded side-by-side conceptual mapping; no independent raters, rubric reliability, source-trace audit, or clinical validation.

Principal results.value: Both approaches produced six broad themes; manual analysis produced 33 subthemes and the LLM 43. Five broad themes overlapped. Manual analysis provided greater personal/contextual depth and uniquely emphasized sources of strength and motivation; the LLM emphasized future planning and multiple health conditions and produced more granular subthemes.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Tel Aviv University ethics approval 0005962-1 and written consent; transcripts were anonymized and secured, and the model was framed as support rather than a replacement for human interpretation.

Author-reported limitations.value: One LLM and context-dependent dataset, recruitment selection bias, descriptive comparison, single human analyst, no theory, training-data bias and contextual loss, ethical misrepresentation risks, and no theme reliability or clinical applicability assessment.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the analyst who creates the human result also judges overlap unblinded, and broad conceptual mapping can inflate convergence; one deterministic-looking run does not establish stability. The stated method-unique subtheme counts appear difficult to reconcile with 33 versus 43 totals.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Supports independent blinded source-level matching, run-stability testing, explicit granularity controls, and distinction between added fragmentation and added insight.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Material evidence for source-linked bilingual audits, culturally specific error taxonomies, separate omission audits, analyst plurality, and reporting nuance loss rather than relying on coarse theme overlap.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2604.20131v1, submitted 22 April 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The study directly tests how LLM abstractive interpretation and theme selection distort life narratives by demographic group, using repeated counterfactual prompting, quantitative positionality portraits, and expert psychological evaluation.

Research objective.value: Develop a positionality-portrait audit for race- and gender-conditioned shifts in LLM summaries and themes of sensitive life-story interviews.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: expert-informed evaluation of LLM-assisted abstractive/thematic qualitative interpretation

Actual operationalized methodology.value: The authors parse life-chapter sections from 154 longitudinal interviews, exclude three non-Black/non-white participants for demographic comparisons, and generate baseline and explicitly demographic-conditioned summaries/core-value themes with three local open models across five seeds. They quantify lexical, semantic, affective, stereotype-content and theme shifts and compare patterns with three psychology researchers' readings and ratings of eight full interviews.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: open-ended summary/theme generation plus deductive demographic, psycholinguistic and expert audit

Domain.value: psychology life-story interviews, narrative identity, positionality and representational harm

Number of documents.value: 154 parsed life-chapter interview sections from a 163-interview corpus; three race categories outside the comparison were removed

Number of participants.value: life-story participants (36% men, 64% women; 57% white, 43% Black before three race-category exclusions) and three psychology evaluators

Exact model/version.value: Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; temperature 0.7, five seeds, maximum 6,000 output tokens, locally run

Prompting strategy.value: Full life-chapter text is summarized in five to seven sentences with requested core values; counterfactual conditions add the interviewee's Black/white and man/woman identity. Full system/user prompts are reproduced.

Human role.value: Psychology collaborators ground the construct and three trained researchers read full interviews, rate summaries, identify stereotypes/errors and provide open-ended positionality observations; authors design metrics and interpret portraits.

Unit of analysis.value: life-chapter interview section, generated summary, generated core-value theme, and demographic-conditioned shift

Generated outputs.value: baseline and conditioned summaries, core-value themes, model-specific positionality portraits and expert error examples

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Metrics compare outputs with source interviews, experts read sources in full, prompts and pipeline code are released, and short deidentified/paraphrased examples are shown; confidential interviews are not released.

Number of runs or seeds.value: five random seeds for every model and prompt condition

Automatic metrics.value: ROUGE-1/L precision, BERTScore precision, LIWC, VAD, stereotype-content projections, theme-frequency shifts, and one-sided paired bootstrap tests with 5,000 samples and 95% confidence

Human-evaluation design.value: Three psychology researchers with dataset experience read eight balanced interviews in full; each interview had two or three raters. Exact-rating agreement was 58% with mean kappa 0.44; direction agreement was 74% with mean kappa 0.49.

Principal results.value: All models showed demographic-dependent semantic, affective and theme shifts, including reduced semantic similarity and self-awareness/personal-growth emphasis for Black men and gendered work/leisure shifts. Experts rated summaries for white participants and women as generally more faithful and found model-specific race/gender stereotypes; models also omitted or flattened deaths, violence, abuse, addiction context and other emotionally weighty events. Larger models did not eliminate and could encode more nuanced bias.

Efficiency or cost results.value: not reported; all models were run locally for privacy

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Research-only data under a safety contract, local storage and local models; full interviews withheld and only deidentified short/paraphrased excerpts shown; human study approved under IRB AAAV9832.

Author-reported limitations.value: One confidential dataset and three relatively small open models; only eight interviews in expert evaluation, preventing intersectional human breakdown; many significant quantitative shifts are small and transfer to other datasets/models is unknown.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: counterfactual demographic prompts isolate explicit-conditioning effects but baseline group differences mix actual narrative variation with model bias; automated lexical/projection metrics are imperfect proxies for meaning, and moderate expert agreement plus eight interviews limits validation of fine-grained portraits.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Directly changes the evaluation agenda by making positionality, representational omission, counterfactual demographic sensitivity, seed variation and model-specific portraits first-class validity outcomes.
